clue.text: Obstacle for canoeists paddling initially in storms

indicators.note: in places the paddling letter within the word for storms

parts.note: to storm a place is to raid it, so storms gives raids

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of paddling

explanation.surface: Canoeists paddling through bad weather meet trouble on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast, broken stretches of white water are a hazard that canoeists must negotiate.

clue.text: Programme shown before about cultural material

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
peat is the material used in cultivation, a growing medium for plants

explanation.surface: A broadcast schedule mentions a programme seen earlier about cultural matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultural' looks like arts and culture, but here it means horticultural: peat is used for growing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a broadcast of a programme already aired, a familiar television sense.

clue.text: Someone rich and powerful put car lot into redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters of put and car lot are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tycoon puts a used-car lot into a property redevelopment scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy person whose money gives them political influence is a member of a ruling elite of wealth.

clue.text: Appropriate behaviour for environmentalist breaking into oil storage facility

indicators.note: breaking into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a drum is a barrel in which oil is stored
eco is short for an ecological campaigner

explanation.surface: An eco-protester breaks into an oil depot, hardly appropriate behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety, or behaviour in keeping with good taste, is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Critical remark makes good chap flutter

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a reliable, decent person
to bat the eyelids is to flutter them

explanation.surface: A nasty comment sets a decent fellow's heart fluttering.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone 'a brick' is dated British praise for a loyal, helpful person.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a missile thrown at someone, it now means a piece of harsh criticism.

clue.text: Games played between drinks in fund-raising event

indicators.note: between places the rearranged letters with one drink on each side

parts.note: rum is a spirit, one drink
ale is beer, the other drink

indicators.note: played says the letters of games are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Party games are held between rounds of drinks at a charity fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' looks like part of the party scene, but it is the signal to rearrange the word before it; one clue word, 'drinks', supplies both outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble of donated goods sold to raise money for a cause is this kind of event.

clue.text: Relative to perform dance getting up in church

indicators.note: in puts the turned dance within the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tango is to perform a particular Latin dance

explanation.surface: A relative gets up to dance in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting up' suits a down answer, where reading upwards means backwards; the dance is read that way before going inside the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words or people sharing a common origin are kin, as in related languages.

clue.text: Model aircraft material a piece of cake to set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a slab is a thick slice of cake

explanation.surface: Building a model aircraft is said to be a piece of cake to put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like the idiom for something easy; it is A plus SLAB, reversed by 'to set up' to give the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This very light tropical wood is the classic material for building model planes.

clue.text: Keepers of birds gobbling first bit of nutrition

indicators.note: gobbling means eating, so the birds' word swallows the letter

parts.note: turkeys are large farmyard birds

indicators.note: first bit of picks the opening letter of nutrition

explanation.surface: Bird-keepers watch their turkeys gobble up the first bit of feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gobbling' is apt for turkeys, but here it signals one piece swallowing another.
explanation.definitionFit: Jailers who hold the keys to the cells are prison keepers in older usage.

clue.text: Page puts on a little weight in spring

indicators.note: puts on places the page letter before the weight in the across answer

parts.note: an ounce is a small imperial unit of weight

explanation.surface: A page boy puts on a little weight in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap suddenly upon prey, as a cat does, is to spring at it.

clue.text: Runner is more self-satisfied going round lake

indicators.note: going round means the comparative word encircles the lake letter

parts.note: smugger is the comparative of smug, self-satisfied
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A jogger grows more pleased with themself as they circuit the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it means a person who runs contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun-runner or rum-runner is someone who brings illegal goods across borders.

clue.text: Biblical books could make chap pray, getting old inside

indicators.note: inside places the old letter within the rearranged letters
could make says the letters of chap pray can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A man at prayer reads from old scripture books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could make' rearranges CHAP PRAY, and 'getting old inside' puts O within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the scriptural texts excluded from the accepted canon, printed separately in some Bibles.

clue.text: Magazines spell silica wrong, missing an i

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: wrong says the remaining letters are put in the wrong order
missing means one i is taken away from silica

parts.note: the letter i, one of the two in silica

explanation.surface: A proofreader complains that magazines misspell silica, dropping an i.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like spelling, but it means a stretch of time; 'missing an i' drops one of silica's two i's before 'wrong' jumbles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Publications issued at regular intervals, such as weekly or monthly journals.

clue.text: A shortage, unfortunately

parts.note: a lack is a shortage or want

explanation.surface: A shortage is unfortunate news.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic exclamation expresses regret, like alas or sadly.

clue.text: Oxford detective with not so much in bank, cruelly

indicators.note: in places the detective and the smaller amount within the verb for bank

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
Inspector Morse is the detective of the Oxford-set British TV series
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse, with little money in the bank, is treated harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'bank on'. Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and a long-running British TV drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without pity or mercy means acting relentlessly and harshly.

clue.text: Small, with damn clean brickwork?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
and means with, in addition to
blast is a mild curse, like damn

explanation.surface: Someone cursing quietly while cleaning brick walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit fired at high pressure is one way to scour masonry; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: I'm consuming Delia's cooking seeking perfection

indicators.note: consuming means the first piece swallows the rearranged letters
cooking means mixing up, so the letters of Delia's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats Delia Smith's cooking in pursuit of the perfect meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook; here the 's counts as a letter in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The pursuit of high principles and perfect standards is the outlook this word describes.

clue.text: Decline to put off one formal speech

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
I is the Roman numeral for one
an oration is a formal public address

explanation.surface: Someone declines to postpone a formal speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb (refuse), but it is the noun meaning a falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: A worsening or falling away in condition is a gradual decay.

clue.text: Restrain scoundrel to suffer again

parts.note: to rein in is to restrain, as with a horse
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Holding back a villain only causes more suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty a second time is to bring it on oneself once more.

clue.text: Childhood, as imagined

definitions.meaning: the earliest years of life, babyhood
split as two words, the phrase means existing only in the imagination

explanation.surface: Childhood as we fondly picture it.
explanation.definitionFit: The early period of life, and also, read as two words, something held only in one's fancy.

clue.text: Booze round North Dakota in drunken spree

indicators.note: round means the drink encircles the state letters

parts.note: beer is booze
ND is the postal abbreviation for the US state of North Dakota

explanation.surface: Drinking across North Dakota on a boozy spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild bout of heavy drinking is a binge, in informal British usage.

clue.text: French friend's entertaining at fiddle

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ami is French for friend; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A French friend is entertaining guests by playing the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like cheating or fidgeting, but it is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins made by the Amati family of Cremona are prized instruments, so one is a fiddle.

clue.text: An attack of illness on the go

parts.note: a bout is a spell or attack of an illness, as of flu

explanation.surface: A bout of illness strikes someone who is always busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and moving around, active rather than bedridden, is to be up and active.

clue.text: Fan belief stirring description of God

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of fan belief into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan's stirring faith in a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Too great to be expressed in words, the term is used of the divine, beyond utterance.

clue.text: Armoured battleship can lord it endlessly at sea

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of it is dropped, leaving only its first
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naval vessel can lord it over others on the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century warship protected by iron plates was known by this name.

clue.text: International relief includes pence still owed

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, is the international body
P is the abbreviation for pence in British money
aid is relief given to those in need

explanation.surface: An international aid budget includes pennies that are still outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill not yet settled is outstanding, money that has not been handed over.

clue.text: Driver to get damp going round hill

indicators.note: going round means the damp word encircles the hill

parts.note: moist means slightly wet, damp
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A driver gets wet circling a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drives a car is a car user on the road.

clue.text: Bill losing head swallows unknown shellfish

indicators.note: swallows means the trimmed word takes the unknown inside it
losing head drops the opening letter

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Bill, a headless diner, swallows a mysterious shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a notice. Without its head it is OSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve mollusc prized as a delicacy, often eaten raw.
